Generate Stratified or Simple Random Sample Indicators

Source: R/sampling_functions.R
generate_sample_index.Rd

Given a population data frame, generates a binary vector indicating which units are selected for human coding. Supports simple random sampling (SRS), stratified proportional allocation, and custom per-stratum sample sizes.

generate_sample_index(
  dat,
  n_code,
  Z = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  p_tx = 0.5,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

dat

Data frame containing the population.

n_code

Sample size specification. If a single number, units are allocated proportionally across strata (and treatment arms if Z is specified). If a vector matching the number of strata-by-treatment cells, specifies exact counts per cell.

Z

Character string naming the treatment indicator column, or NULL to ignore treatment assignment. When specified, sampling is done within substrata defined by crossing strata with treatment. Default is NULL.

strata

Character string naming the stratification column, or NULL for SRS (all units in one stratum). Default is NULL.

p_tx

Numeric between 0 and 1. Proportion of the total sample allocated to the treatment arm when Z is specified and n_code is a single number. If NULL, uses the observed treatment proportion. Default is 0.5.

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducibility.

Value

An integer vector of length nrow(dat) with values 0 (not sampled) or 1 (sampled).

See also

generate_observed_sample for a wrapper that also masks unsampled outcomes, calc_sampling_weights for computing the implied sampling probabilities.
